name: glassdoor/jobs
description: Search Glassdoor job listings by keyword and location, with title, company, rating, salary estimate, location and posting age.

q.description: Parameter defines the job search query, like the job title or keyword search box of Glassdoor (e.g., `software engineer`, `nurse`, or `Python`). `q`, `location`, or `employer_id` is required.

radius.description: Parameter defines the maximum distance from `location`, in miles in the United States and in kilometers elsewhere, like the Distance filter of Glassdoor. It defaults to `25` for cities. Available options: `0` - Within 0 `5` - Within 5 `10` - Within 10 `15` - Within 15 `25` - Within 25 `50` - Within 50 `100` - Within 100

remote.description: Parameter defines whether to only show remote jobs, like the Remote only filter of Glassdoor. It can be set to `true` or `false` (default).

job_type.description: Parameter defines the type of the jobs. Available options: `full_time` - Full-time `part_time` - Part-time `contract` - Contract

location.description: Parameter defines the location of the jobs, like the location search box of Glassdoor: a city, state or country (e.g., `New York, NY`, `Texas`, `London`, or `Germany`). We use the first location Glassdoor suggests with that name, or else its first suggestion, and the JSON response shows it in `search_information.location`. Without it, Glassdoor searches jobs in the United States. Without `q`, Glassdoor doesn't search some countries (e.g., `Canada` or `Germany`), and the JSON response has an error. `q`, `location`, or `employer_id` is required.

easy_apply.description: Parameter defines whether to only show jobs you can apply to on Glassdoor, like the Easy Apply only filter of Glassdoor. It can be set to `true` or `false` (default).

max_salary.description: Parameter defines the maximum yearly salary of the jobs, in the currency of `location` (e.g., `150000`).

min_rating.description: Parameter defines the minimum Glassdoor rating of the companies, from `1` to `4` (e.g., `4` for companies rated 4.0 and up).

min_salary.description: Parameter defines the minimum yearly salary of the jobs, in the currency of `location` (e.g., `100000`).

date_posted.description: Parameter defines the maximum number of days since the jobs were posted. Available options: `1` - Last day `3` - Last 3 days `7` - Last week `14` - Last 2 weeks `30` - Last month

employer_id.description: Parameter defines the Glassdoor ID of the company to show the jobs of (e.g., `9079` for Google). It is the number after `E` in Glassdoor company URLs (e.g., https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/Google-Reviews-E9079.htm), and the `company_id` of jobs and `employer_id` of our Glassdoor Companies API results. `q`, `location`, or `employer_id` is required.

json_restrictor.description: Parameter defines the fields you want to include in the output, reducing payload size for faster response. See the JSON Restrictor documentation for more details.

next_page_token.description: Parameter defines the token of the next page of results. Up to `30` results are returned per page, for up to `30` pages. The token is in the JSON response: `the API_pagination.next_page_token`. Use it with the same other parameters as the search it comes from.

seniority_level.description: Parameter defines the seniority level of the jobs. Available options: `internship` - Internship `entry_level` - Entry level `mid_senior_level` - Mid-senior level `director` - Director `executive` - Executive

# Glassdoor Jobs

Search Glassdoor job listings by keyword and location, with title, company, rating, salary estimate, location and posting age.

## Request

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.sandbase.ai/v1/api/glassdoor/jobs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SANDBASE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"q": "data engineer"}'
```

The result is returned in `outputs[0].data` as structured JSON.
